# fccexam

**Practice tests for the US FCC commercial radio licence exams**

- **Version recorded:** 1.0.7
- **Categories:** `exams`
- **Upstream:** <https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/fccexam>

## What it does

Practice questions for the FCC commercial radio operator licence elements -- the General Radiotelephone Operator Licence and the associated endorsements -- drawn from the published pools.

## Why you would want it

These are not the amateur exams. The GROL is what a technician maintaining aviation, marine or broadcast transmitters needs, and it comes up for amateurs who work professionally around radio. The Debian Blend's own note on this package says the same thing, because the confusion is common.

## Before it will work

None.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`morse`](../profiles/morse.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install fccexam --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## Known problems

Frequently mistaken for the amateur exam tool; that is `hamexam`. The pool snapshot caveat applies here too -- Ubuntu and Kali carry 1.0.8 against 1.0.7 elsewhere (measured 2026-08-28).
